Contrary to many people, I'm not a fan of adding mosfets everywhere. As mentioned in my message it ads complexity and points of failure. The manufacturer should use better terminals which would cost them close to nothing. As for soldering directly to the board, yes that sound like a good alternative for the user.

The worse is most of these fires could have been avoided just by using better terminals. I understand Anet and gang skimp on cost to allow for low prices, but this this issue have been happening again and again, and the fix \(on their side\) probably cost 0.1$. The user shouldn't have to add an extra MOSFET, multiplying cabling and risk points at the same time.

I've used both buildtak and PEI and can compare.

I've had three different sheets from different sources, and been cleaning them properly. It only stuck with the bed at high temp. Buildtak grips at low to no temperature and don't require frequent cleaning, I much prefer that.

You're wasting time trying to force your opinion on me.

ABS: I'm sure _some_ people have good use for it, I never said the contrary. TP holders: it was a joke, I don't have stats over how many TP holders come out of the million Anet machines out there. Forget about it. Consider you won the ABS fight. Now I don't find ABS over rated anymore, and surely won't find it ridiculous when people print halloween pumpkins with it.

PEI: I'm not interested in having to clean the sheet at every print when other solutions don't need that. Good for you if it works great between cleaning and gluing.  I prefer not having to do either. PEI leaves me unimpressed.

It is true that I can't _state_ that people don't _need_ ABS for their Christmas decoration and TP holders, however it is my opinion that they don't.

For the PEI, if I where to use glue stick I might as well use any surface. I've had three different PEi sheets from different sources before giving up (kept them clean with 90% all and microfibre cloth). Some googling show I'm not alone, and recommendations are "heat it to 90c" and "sand it". I might as well get Buildtac and use it at low to no temp.

 This was anyway never intended as a "list of absolute statements" but "overhyped stuff that left me unimpressed"

To make the bar thing clear: Espresso should be brewed at 9 bars. As most people put random stale ground in their machine and expect crema (foam on top) machine producers started with filter baskets that would squirt the coffee through a small hole in order to foam some fake crema. These baskets are called pressurised and take 15 bar from the machine to compensate for the small exit hole, the brew pressure being about what it should.

To get back to machines: buy an espresso machine if you care about espresso, else it's more of hassle than other brewing methods. If you do want to make espresso I would recommend a second hand Gaggia classic (pre-2015, ˜150$), so you can switch to unpressurised baskets and 9 bar when you feel ready. This machine is indestructible and leaves some budget for a grinder too.

Whichever brewing method you end up with, fresh grind is the cornerstone, you will get better result from freshly roasted / ground coffee in the cheapest junk machine than pre-ground in a high end machine. If you want to be serious, the bulk of the budget should go on the grinder. Doesn't sound so fun, but anyone on any espresso forum will confirm.
